runs.name: DTE Energy Company; NYSE DTE, SEC CIK 0000936340, Michigan, 10-K filer jointly with DTE Electric Company; parent of DTE Electric (about 2.3 million electric customers in southeastern Michigan) and DTE Gas (about 1.4 million gas customers in Michigan), rate-regulated, plus two non-utility segments, DTE Vantage and Energy Trading; Oracle 1.4 GW and Google 1.0 GW data-centre supply agreements, $1.0B junior subordinated debentures 2026-06-18, DT Midstream spun off inside the balance-sheet window; the 10-K names no rival, CMS, WEC and Xcel chosen as a CONVENTION of the run
runs.entry: Price **$129.73** (close 2026-10-16, aggregator, flagged). Shares **208,088,069** on the 10-Q cover (0000936340-26-000146); market cap $26,995M. Sovereign **5.43%**, US Treasury 30-year par yield 2026-10-16. Read from the 10-K FY2025 (0000936340-26-000054), the 10-Ks FY2023, FY2021, FY2019 and FY2017, the 10-Q of 2026-06-30 (0000936340-26-000146), the proxy (0000936340-26-000062), the Oracle and Google 8-Ks, the debenture 8-K and the $1.5B equity distribution 8-K; lines of evidence derived by the analyst from Items 1, 1A and 7, stated in the run file; `tools/run.py` UNRESEARCHED on DTE's own capital-spending labels, every figure taken by hand from the filed statements. **Q1 IN**: DTE Electric decides at 66% of 2021 to 2025 segment net income ($4,822M of $7,265M; Vantage 10%, Energy Trading 6%); authorized return 9.9% re-affirmed by the MPSC on 2026-02-19 against 10.75% asked. **Q2 IN**: a statutory franchise, retail access capped by Michigan law at 10% of sales and running at 10% for three years; protects a fair regulated return, DTE Electric 9.8% on its own equity in 2025; regulated return carried to Q3 as a second best. **Q3 WEIGHS AGAINST**: 6.5% pre-tax on tangible capital, 7.7% on added capital; compulsory spending 2.2 to 2.6 times depreciation every year, $6.8B planned for 2026 against about $3.9B of operating cash. **Q4 WEIGHS AGAINST** (no confusion, no suspicion): ten balance sheets read, debt $11.8B to $27.6B while equity rose only $9.0B to $12.1B, debt share of capital 57% to 69%; parent equity ($12,154M) below DTE Electric's own ($12,426M); regulatory assets doubled to $8.2B; featured operating earnings exclude recurring disallowances; guidance. **Q5 integrity IN on a close call**: the bonus paid its 200% maximum on adjusted operating EPS of $7.36 where reported EPS of $7.03 was below the $7.09 threshold; ability weighs slightly for. **Q6 Part A and Part B WEIGH AGAINST**: about 60% of earnings paid out while $500M to $600M of new shares a year are planned for 2026 to 2028; retention $1.07 of market value per $1 retained; unsettled forward sales of about 3.7M shares at $141.96 to $144.41. **Q7 OUT**, equity-only central under Q7, The regulated utility, 2022 to 2025: owner cash **$1,289M a year** equity-only maintenance-only (depreciation with nuclear fuel as the maintenance guess, stock pay deducted), **$533M** after all spending with $7,667M of net new long-term debt credited at DTE's own debt share (the filing states no allowed structure; the cap did not bind); growth cut under (f) to utility revenue growth of 3.53%; value range **$114.06 to $123.78 a share equity-only** (bottom no growth, top the growth case at 5.43%; at ten percent the growth case falls below the no-growth case, the growth bought costing more than it returns, recorded under (e)); literal window 2021 to 2025 beside, $117.42 / $113.94; generous maintenance (the filed base-infrastructure plan) beside, 6.2%; expected return 4.8% to 5.2% at the price, below the 5.43% bond; fair price **$59.23 equity-only, central**, -$41.55 all-equity, not positive; ten percent at the price needs 12.9% a year growth for ten years. Q8 to Q12 not reached. After the stop, facts recorded, not weighed: interest coverage 1.7x in the first half of 2026; Fermi 2 decommissioning trusts $2,552M; REF guarantees up to $201M. Competitors: none named in the 10-K; CMS, WEC and Xcel chosen as a CONVENTION; return on equity 2016 to 2025 mean DTE 11.3% (lifted by parent borrowing), CMS 13.8%, WEC 11.8% (eight years), Xcel 10.4%; regulated-level returns, no breakaway; peer figures XBRL transcription. Strongest evidence against: compulsory spending at more than twice depreciation funded with debt and new shares while 60% of earnings is paid out; the adjusted figure the bonus is paid on. Commits 721fe7b5 (template), d0764ccf (Step 0, Q1), a05581c7 (Q2), 1db6aac3 (Q3 and Q4 together, declared), 4d70b0b6 (Q5 and Q6 together, declared), d876563d (Q7 with the Q6 write-back, box, self-audit, gaps); Q7 arithmetic computed during Step 0 under the COMPUTATION heading and not used before Q7, declared in the self-audit. Position note filled at the fold: not held. Contamination declared: a `Test Runs/` listing showing other 2026-10-18 run names (CMS, Ameren, AEP, Dominion and others) and an addendum name, the Dominion fold's commit subjects, the adopted utility case's list of sixteen utilities that closed OUT, memory index lines; none opened or used. Citations: the analyst's `check_run.py` 0 problems; the dispatcher's `_dispatcher_cite_check.py` no missing id, 93 adjacent quoted fragments, 4 flagged and all read (line-wrapped fragments and a transcript dash artifact, the words in their rows), **no citation slip**. No tracked research file over 200 KB. check_framework PASS. **For the operator** (the analyst's framework notes): (1) the utility credit's "debt raised" gross or net (net used); (2) whose debt share, the parent's or the regulated subsidiary's; (3) how the credited debt splits between maintenance and growth spending inside the maintenance-only case; (4) a spin-off inside the window, the specifics covering acquisitions and mergers only; (5) "sales" under (f) for a company with a gross-revenue trading arm (utility revenue used); the rest in the run file's seven items. Could not get: the regulator's allowed capital structure (DTE's own debt share used); WEC equity for 2018 and 2019; the expiry of Vantage's tax credits. Armed at the equity-only fair price.
runs.narr: OUT at Q7 (DTE Energy, DTE; Michigan regulated electricity and gas; Q1 IN, DTE Electric deciding at 66%; Q2 IN on the statute, retail access capped at 10%; Q3 against, 7.7% pre-tax on added capital, spending 2.2 to 2.6 times depreciation; Q4 against, debt share 57% to 69%, parent equity below the utility's; Q5 integrity IN on a close call, the bonus at maximum on adjusted EPS where GAAP missed the threshold; Q6 against, 60% paid out while new shares are sold; owner cash $1,289M a year equity-only maintenance-only, $533M after all spending with $7,667M of debt credited; value range $114.06 to $123.78 equity-only vs $129.73, best case 6.2%; fair $59.23 equity-only, armed (-$41.55 all-equity, not positive); no citation slip; not held; framework gaps for the operator: debt raised gross or net, whose debt share, the credit inside the maintenance case, a spin-off in the window, sales for a trading arm)
